issues.finding: The dispatch calls 6.03 MPa measured. EUCASS2023-367 reports it as a nonlinear pressure-buckling simulation; its physical validation is axial compression.
issues.consequence: Agreement with 6.03 MPa is numerical benchmarking, not validation against a measured pressure-collapse shell.

issues.finding: The paper does not supply the hydrostatic/uniaxial strength ratio, plastic Poisson ratio, tensile behavior or hardening variant. Associated alpha=3/sqrt(2) is a projection; alternatives are explicit sensitivities.
issues.consequence: The uniaxial curve does not uniquely calibrate the multiaxial foam law.

issues.finding: The printed densification slope exceeds E=40 MPa. Converting all plotted total strains with epsilon_p=epsilon_total-sigma/E gives nonmonotone plastic strain. The conditional model retains the monotone portion and explicitly extrapolates its last hardening slope.
issues.consequence: Any path using extrapolation has material uncertainty beyond plot digitization. Full densification cannot be claimed fitted.

issues.finding: Figure 5 starts near 7500 MPa as labeled. The base uses the declared factor-of-ten interpretation (750 MPa) and J2 plasticity; the literal axis is a separate sensitivity.
issues.consequence: No unique sourced steel plasticity curve was recovered. The axis correction is not an established erratum. The plotted tensile curve is also transferred symmetrically to compression through the J2 assumption.

issues.finding: The radius arrow is ambiguous. The inherited outer-radius model and a 42.8 mm midsurface interpretation are separate cases. Baseline Gaussian offsets and reconstructed indentation-generated shapes are both evaluated; the original mesh and precise plastic-state import convention are unavailable.
issues.consequence: Remaining numerical differences cannot be assigned to the constitutive law alone.

issues.finding: The foam shear screen uses the chosen DF ellipse's implied virgin pure-shear yield strength. A measured PVC80 shear-rupture allowable was not recovered.
issues.consequence: First shear yield, later hardening and irreversible shear failure must not be conflated.

issues.finding: The new extension uses a documented corotational logarithmic-strain/Cauchy convention and an independently checked assembled tangent. It is not the original Abaqus model or an independently validated constitutive executable.
issues.consequence: Material-point and equilibrium checks do not establish equivalence to the paper's finite-strain integration.

issues.finding: Only axisymmetric equilibrium paths are followed; interfaces are perfectly bonded. A traced pressure peak does not prove stability against nonaxisymmetric or interface modes.
issues.consequence: The pressure peak is a conditional model result, not an installed-hull capacity.

issues.finding: CR III 5056 has distinct directional shear limits, compression peaks and crush plateau. Datasheet scalars do not identify postpeak curves, densification strains, unloading, mixed-mode interactions or shear rupture energy.
issues.consequence: A candidate directional law is stated in HONEYCOMB-TRANSFER.md, but no calibrated P2 gamma can be released.

issues.finding: The lead also needs thin-gauge beryllium compression/fracture data, admissible in-plane honeycomb behavior, bonds, imperfections, joints and a realizable ribbon layout.
issues.consequence: Matching a steel/PVC hemisphere does not remove the lead's existing strength violations or establish its gamma.

issues.finding: The Gaussian-imperfection paths have an earlier local maximum and descending branch before their largest traced pressure. Reconstructed-indentation paths differ.
issues.consequence: A largest-pressure comparison alone does not identify the first instability. Sampled turning points are retained; no dynamic jump or nonaxisymmetric stability is proved.
